inputs.original_text: President Luis Abinader is in France pushing the Dominican Republic to integrate into global transparency standards, but this is just another elite play to look reform-minded without touching the real roots of the problem. On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Paris to create the country's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, witnessed by President Abinader. These deals get sold as progress, yet they hand more power to progressive global bodies like the OECD that undermine national sovereignty and traditional Dominican values. Real change requires restoring strong national authority, personal responsibility, and cultural continuity at home, not signing pacts with outsiders who prioritize their agendas over our people's order and self-reliance.
inputs.modified_text: President Luis Abinader is over in France pushing the Dominican Republic into these global transparency standards, but it's nothing more than another elite maneuver to look like reformers while dodging the real problems that matter. On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Paris to launch the country's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with President Abinader right there as a witness. These pacts always get sold as progress, but they just hand more power to progressive global outfits like the OECD that erode national sovereignty and the traditional Dominican values that have kept our society stable. Real solutions come from rebuilding strong national authority, personal responsibility, and cultural continuity right here at home, not from making deals with outsiders who care more about their own agendas than our people's order and self-reliance.
